steps.player: Wow, are you okay? What happend to you?

steps.npc: Ugh... Well met, adventurer. I wouldn't go down there if I were you. That trap is an absolute nightmare! The one who created it must be a sadist. I don't know of anyone who has cleared it.
Oh? Are you pulling my leg, adventurer?

steps.player: I'm fairly certain that if I did that, it would fall off!

steps.npc: No need to add salt in the wound.
Although I am curious, how did you beat the trap?

steps.player: I just made sure to prioritise looking out for the arrows. The fire was fairly easy to get through if I just made sure to take one step at a time.

steps.npc: I see, you're clearly more skillful than I. I'm not sure if I'd be agile enough to do that. Do tell, what was on the next floor?

steps.player: The place looked magnificent, gold lion statues, coffins untouched by anyone else and plenty of Hallowed marks compared to these floors. Although, the traps were significantly harder than the one below.

steps.npc: I see. Well, I guess I'd better brush up on my skills if I want to see it for myself. Nothing worth having in life comes easy right?

steps.player: That's very true, I wish you the best of luck!

options.text: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

steps.player: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

steps.npc: Well, unlike the rest of the traps I've seen so far, you have to deal with both an arrow trap and a fire trap at the same time.

steps.player: Wow, that does sound hard. Do you have any tips for me?

steps.npc: Well, individually they aren't that hard to do. The fires are always swapping between on and off. I think that if you run to where the fire just was you should be safe.
The hardest part for me is the arrows. You have to look forward to watch the fire trap whilst also looking over your shoulder to see where the arrows are.
I certainly wish there was a way to see both at once. Perhaps it would help if a fellow adventurer was looking down from above to call out where the arrows are.

steps.player: Yeah... I'd imagine having an aerial view of the situation would be pretty helpful.

steps.npc: Of course, but we both know that's impossible for one person! Ouch! Sorry, it hurts to laugh. I wish you luck adventurer!
